thread:
lina (product): Quick decision: what do we expose to clients when we route to a lower-cost compatibility variant? Need concise contract and console telemetry labels.

sam (eng-platform): Proposal: always return HTTP 200, include minimal `route` metadata in the JSON body, and make a verbose opt-in for warnings. No new status codes.

tess (eng-runtime): Runtime emits ROUTE_COMPAT internally. Public mapping: route.kind="degraded" or "primary"; route.variant label = "compat"|"cached"|"lite". We'll attach trace tag rw.route_kind and rw.variant_label and a counter rw.variant.count.

lee (devex): UI: per-route pill "Degraded (compat)" with percent; tooltip "Served from compatibility variant to preserve latency". No banner unless >10%. Allow org-level toggle to show warnings in API responses.

nav (eng-sre): Telemetry/alerts: emit rw.variant.rate_pct and rw.variant.latency_p95. Alert: warn at 4% sustained 6h, critical at 20% sustained 24h. Nightly job samples degraded responses for QA checks.

sam (eng-platform): API snippet: header `X-RW-Route: degraded|primary|cached` and body snippet "\"route\":{\"kind\":\"degraded\",\"variant\":\"compat\"}". Config per-org `expose_route: none|labels|full`. Hosted default = labels only.

lina (product): Tone: avoid "error" or "fallback" in customer copy. Use "compatibility variant" and reassuring language. Rollout: internal 48h -> alpha opt-in -> GA. Owners: sam RFC, lee console, nav alerts, tess runtime.

all: +1
